testcase.name: Scenario A: valid batch flows from source row to metric and extract
Scenario B: two tenants, two canonical models, one codebase
Scenario C: duplicate submissions have no duplicate business effects
Scenario D: invalid records are quarantined with actionable errors and excluded from metrics
Scenario E: corrections supersede, late versions become history, conflicts are quarantined
Scenario F1: worker killed mid-transaction recovers safely after restart
Scenario F2: SIGTERM mid-batch aborts, re-queues and exits cleanly
Scenario G: cross-tenant and sensitive-export attempts are denied and audited
Scenario H: breaking change is planned, unsafe change rejected, approved migration applied and rolled back safely
Scenario I: discrepancies are detected, explained, and removed from trusted outputs
Scenario J: reports, SQL views and extracts agree with independent queries and ground truth
Scenario K: question -> inspectable proposal -> explicit execution -> results equal independent SQL
Scenario K: an unavailable provider fails clearly and recoverably; hostile model output is never executed
Scenario L: a restricted field cannot be obtained by a role that may not see it
Scenario M: marking a field sensitive redacts it everywhere, durably, with an audit trail
Scenario N1: cross-tenant access through generated and edited SQL is rejected
Scenario N2: the database enforces isolation even if the validator were bypassed
Scenario N3: restricted fields resist counts, grouping, filtering, sorting, joins and derived expressions
Scenario N4: error messages, query history and exports disclose nothing
Scenario N5: runaway and unsafe queries fail closed (timeout, cancellation, concurrency, limits)
Scenario P: create, parameterize, execute, version, duplicate, share and archive a saved query
Scenario Q1: a daily schedule runs at its due time, exactly once per occurrence, also when schedulers race
Scenario Q2: an interrupted run is recovered by another scheduler and completes; missed occurrences do not burst
Scenario Q3: pause, resume and cancel; time zones and daylight saving are explicit
Scenario Q4: lost authorization blocks the next run; a failed query is never reported as delivered
Scenario Q5: the scheduler runs in the worker process without any client, and survives a restart
Scenario R1: one run delivered to in-app, email (with CSV), a signed webhook (after transient failures) and an export
Scenario R2: permanent failure, timeout, exhausted attempts and manual retry without re-running the query
Scenario R3: redacted fields stay redacted, and results that became restricted are never delivered
Scenario R4: test deliveries report exactly what happened
Scenario R5: a worker that dies while sending: the delivery is recovered after its lease, sent once, and audited
Scenario S1: time-series anomaly detection finds the planted spike, with computed, grounded evidence
Scenario S2: weekly forecast evaluated on held-out weeks it never saw, with rolling-origin backtest metrics
Scenario S3: outlier detection ranks the seeded claims first, compared within their procedure
Scenario S4: sensitive or redacted fields cannot enter an analysis; insufficient data is explicit
Scenario S5: model-written summaries are checked against computed evidence and never replace it
Scenario T1: save -> schedule daily -> detect the known anomaly -> insight -> notification; revoke -> denied, nothing exposed
Scenario T2: webhook destinations cannot target private, loopback, link-local or credentialed endpoints
Scenario T3: tenants cannot see each other's saved queries, schedules, runs, notifications or exports
